steps.intent: Open the reply composer via the Reply link
Write an AI-generated reply tailored to the email into the Message Body (the recorded text is only an example)
Wait for the 'Draft saved' notice confirming auto-save; never press Send
Return to the inbox via 'Back to Inbox' and repeat for the next unread email

dataFlow.field: sender name / email content used to author reply text

successCriteria: After typing the reply, a 'Draft saved' notice appears (div#toast)
The Drafts counter (span#dcount) increases by one per processed email
The Message Body textbox contains the generated reply text
No Send action is performed; the email is not sent
consequentialActions: Send email (Send button in the reply composer) — the widget must never press Send; the user only saved a draft

strategyHints.reason: Opening an email is a client-side click on an inbox row; no network calls observed.
Email content is read from the rendered message view.
Reply composer appears after clicking the Reply link; no network evidence.
Text must be entered into a contenteditable textbox to trigger the app's auto-save.
Save is confirmed only by the live 'Draft saved' toast and draft counter; no network request recorded.
Navigation back uses the 'Back to Inbox' button in the page.

openQuestions: Should the widget draft replies for all unread emails or only the currently open / newest N?
What tone or length should AI-written replies have (e.g. brief acknowledgement vs. detailed answer)?
